_README: Development fixture for the local Convex deployment. Loaded by `bun run seed:dev` (add --worst for the worst-case file, --huge for 1,200 extra enquiries).
GENERATED by scripts/make-dev-seed.ts; edit that, then re-run it.
Numbers are synthetic (99999 xxxxx) but valid Indian mobile format, so normalisation behaves as in production.
`daysAgo` is relative, so a reseed always looks current; `followUpInDays` below zero is overdue.

Everything is published and marked sample, and is replaced the moment the owner edits it. None of it reaches production: convex/devSeed.ts refuses any deployment that is not local or the named hosted dev deployment.

posts.title: How to read the APSC CCE notification before you pick a course
posts.excerpt: The notification answers most week-one questions: syllabus, dates and eligibility. Here is where to find each.
posts.body:
The APSC CCE notification is the single document every plan should start from.

## What to check first

- **Eligibility**: age limits, attempts, domicile rules.
- **Syllabus**: the list of papers, not a coaching brochure.
- **Dates**: application window, prelims, mains.

## Then pick a batch

Once you know the dates, count back: Prelims in March means classes from August.

posts.title: ADRE 3.0 syllabus, section by section
posts.excerpt: General studies, Assam GK, English, maths and reasoning: what each section asks and how much time it deserves.
posts.body:
ADRE rewards breadth.

## General studies

History, polity and geography of India, with Assam in every part.

## English

Grammar and comprehension; twenty minutes a day is enough.

## Maths and reasoning

Speed matters more than difficulty.

posts.title: How the night batch works for people with a job
posts.excerpt: Classes from 8 to 10 PM, recordings the same night, and tests on Sundays.
posts.body:
Half of ICT's APSC students work.

## The week

- Classes Monday to Friday, 8 to 10 PM.
- Recordings on the app by midnight.
- A Sunday test, with results on Monday.

posts.title: The last sixty days before APSC Mains
posts.excerpt: Answer writing every day, one mock a week, and nothing new after day fifty.
posts.body:
Sixty days is enough if you stop collecting material.

## Days 1 to 30

Write two answers a day and get them checked.

## Days 31 to 50

One full mock a week.

## Days 51 to 60

Revise your own notes only.
